{{short description|Geometric plane containing the normal vector of a given surface}}
[[File:Minimal surface curvature planes-en.svg|thumb|300px|right|[[Saddle surface]] with normal planes in directions of principal [[curvature]]s.]]

In [[geometry]], a '''normal plane''' is any plane containing the [[normal vector]] of a [[Surface (topology)|surface]] at a particular point.

The normal plane also refers to the plane that is [[perpendicular]] to the [[tangent vector]] of a [[space curve]]; (this plane also contains the normal vector)  see [[Frenet–Serret formulas]].

== Normal section ==
The '''normal section''' of a [[surface (mathematics)|surface]] at a particular [[point (geometry)|point]] is the [[curve]] produced by the [[intersection]] of that surface with a normal plane.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Ruane|first1=Irving Adler, with diagrams by Ruth Adler; introduction to the Dover edition by Peter|title=A new look at geometry|date=2012|publisher=Dover Publications|location=Mineola, N.Y.|isbn=978-0486498515|page=273|edition=Dover}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EbIAAQAAQBAJ&q=%22Normal+section%22&pg=PA273 |title=A New Look at Geometry |author=Irving Adler |page=273 |date=2013-08-30 |publisher=Courier Corporation |isbn=9780486320496 |accessdate=2016-04-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-LRumtTimYgC&q=%22Normal+section%22+geometry&pg=PA365 |title=Modern Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces with Mathematica, Second ... |author=Alfred Gray |page=365 |date=1997-12-29 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=9780849371646 |accessdate=2016-04-01}}</ref>

The [[curvature]] of the normal section is called the ''[[normal curvature]]''.
If the surface is bow or cylinder shaped, the maximum and the minimum of these curvatures are the ''[[principal curvatures]]''.
If the surface is [[saddle point|saddle shaped]] the maxima of both sides are the principal curvatures.
The product of the principal curvatures is the [[Gaussian curvature]] of the surface (negative for saddle shaped surfaces).
The mean of the principal curvatures is the ''[[mean curvature]]'' of the surface; if (and only if) the mean curvature is zero, the surface is called a ''[[minimal surface]]''.
